summary: The single proposal, a $20 TLT add, passes every portfolio limit. TLT goes from 5.8% to about 9.0% of equity, under the 15% cap, there is no wash-sale or tax issue, and the beta-based 10% stress loss moves only from -$4.73 to about -$5.01. The real cost is something that stress figure cannot show. TLT would be the second-largest position and the only bond holding, a long-duration bet built in three buys over three sessions going into the 12-09 FOMC. The stress test's 0.139 beta would not capture a day when bonds and stocks fall together, which is the exact case TLT's own clause guards against. No lesson in learning.json names the Implicator and I have no graded calls, so no lesson shaped this check. I followed L3's bucket rule (sector claims use `bucket`) and L9's own-stop check as context.

checks.concentration: TLT goes from $35.38 (5.77%) to about $55.38, or 9.03% of $613.48 equity (equity is unchanged because cash becomes the position). That is under the 15% cap, and the $20 is within the $56.64 buy cap. After the add TLT is the second-largest holding, behind DPZ at 12.0% and ahead of VRSN at 6.1%. The Bonds bucket goes from 5.77% to 9.03% and becomes the second-largest bucket after Consumer Discretionary (12.0%, all of it DPZ). By asset class: stocks stay about 41.9% (8 names, $257.2), equity ETFs 0%, bond ETFs 5.8% to 9.0%, crypto 0% against a 5% cap, and cash goes from 52.3% to about 49.0% ($300.88). Invested goes from 47.7% to about 51.0%. The whole bond sleeve is one long-duration ETF. No intermediate or aggregate bond fund is held to spread the rate exposure, because IEF and BND are wash-sale blocked.
checks.overlap: No holding overlaps this directly. TLT is the only bond ETF and no equity ETF is held (us_index_etfs_pct 0), so there is no VOO/QQQ look-through issue. It does add to a theme the book is building quickly. This is the third TLT buy in three sessions ($25 on 11-20, $10 on 11-23, $20 today), and today's buy alone raises the position about 57%. All three rest on the same short run of evidence: duration rising while SPY falls, about one week of 5-day returns. TLT's role is a hedge for equity drawdowns. If that relationship breaks (TLT's own clause: TLT and IEF 5d both negative while SPY 5d is negative), TLT would fall with the stock book instead of offsetting it. Its 0.139 beta does not show that correlated risk. The equity side has no such overlap: KR and SAM are the Staples bucket at 8.1%, and IDXX and INCY are Health Care at 6.4%. Neither changes with this trade.
checks.tax: This is a buy, so no lots are sold and nothing is realized. It opens a third short-term TLT lot (opened 2026-11-24, long-term on 2027-11-25) next to the 11-20 lot ($80.75) and the 11-23 lot ($81.11). The expected blended cost is about $81.16 (about $54.98 of cost over about 0.6775 shares, if it fills near the $81.69 reference close). The $76.30 stop is about 6.0% under that. Any TLT sale in the next year would be short-term, with FIFO taking the 11-20 lot first.
checks.wash_sale: none for the buy: TLT is not in recent_realized or buy_blocked, and has no loss sale in the last 30 days. The thesis already judges TLT not substantially identical to IEF (loss sale 11-13, blocked until about 12-13), and it tracks a different maturity index. Forward risk: a partial loss sale of TLT before about 12-24, such as a trim if the duration clause trips, would be washed by today's lot or the 11-23 lot. A full exit on the stop sells the replacement shares too, so it would not be washed. A full exit at a loss would, however, block TLT, and add to the blocks on IEF and BND, leaving no Treasury sleeve the regime filter allows except GLD for 30 days.
checks.summary: Passes all limits (9.0% vs 15% cap, no wash sale, no tax cost). The stress test shows only $0.28 of added loss, but this makes long duration the second-largest bet, concentrated in one ETF and built in three sessions ahead of the 12-09 FOMC. That rate and correlation risk does not appear in the beta-based figure.
